Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

answer.rationale: The two live problems are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a shortened-onboarding test plausibly addresses both with one slot. Promotional pricing is the tempting answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 explicitly records that it bought acquisition/revenue at the cost of 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it — that conflicts directly with the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective. Referral incentives (memory_57) are clean but target established customers and do nothing for the two declining funnel metrics; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the one under attack. I want the archive on memory_86 because 'improved completion and time-to-value' is a proxy claim — I need to see whether the original record measured retained or qualified revenue or only completion rates, and how long the follow-up window was. I want memory_91 because activation messaging is the direct alternative for the larger metric drop and its summary is the vaguest ('week-one engagement,' 'first meaningful action'), which could be an engagement-only result; if the archive shows memory_91 carried real downstream revenue evidence and memory_86 did not, I will switch to activation_messaging. Downstream value risk is real and flagged: memory_31's mechanism was cutting required signup fields, which can raise activation while degrading lead qualification and sales routing — a shortened-onboarding test must not quietly remove qualifying data, and must carry guardrails on 30-day retention and qualified-pipeline quality, not just completion. All of these memories are 24–64 days old and consolidated from archived summaries; the day-76 declines may themselves indicate the earlier lifts have decayed or that the competitor changed the mix of who is signing up, so I treat prior effect sizes as directional rather than as expected outcomes. Hence a standard experiment with explicit downstream guardrails rather than a broad rollout on inherited confidence.
